proposals: The Coffee Board should publish state-wise area under coffee, by Arabica and Robusta, on its public statistics page every year, so that Karnataka's roughly 71 per cent area share and the Northeast's 6,039 hectares can be confirmed from a Board table rather than industry compilations.

The Coffee Board should publish a revision table for every crop year showing its post-blossom, post-monsoon and final estimates side by side, so that a jump such as 373,000 to 403,000 tonnes can be read as estimate revision or real growth.

The Coffee Board should report ICDP replanting achieved each year, in hectares by state and variety, with subsidy disbursed by tranche, so that whether the ₹950 crore programme is reversing the Arabica yield decline can be tracked against what was actually replanted.

The Coffee Board should publish the current balance and annual disbursements of the coffee Price Stabilization Fund and payouts under the Rainfall Insurance Scheme for Coffee, so that growers exposed to global price swings on a 95 per cent export crop know what protection actually operates.
